**Credit name.** Amund Kristiansen (GitHub @amundsk).

**Claim.** One new upper bound (beyond the case corpus). The side is the certificate's exact rational side, rounded up at 12 places.

| n | New upper bound | Best public before it | Improvement | That bound's source |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 344 | 18.992567544845 | 18.992727809347 | 1.60e-4 | Francisco Couzo, franciscouzo/square-packing@1c17153 `certificates/best/n344.cert` (the same as 964ee2b/#763) |

Comparison: Couzo's index at 1c17153 (which compares the register, open issues and PRs, Mishapolk/square-packing-records and public Kaggle notebooks) and the register's own 344 sources (Fang's two-wedge certificates, Daniel's record hunt 3, Couzo's certificates of 11 October), all higher; no request since #798 reports 344 (checked 25 October).

**Certificate.** Gist https://gist.github.com/amundsk/18ada41ec384b6ff2c96f58b7ce7d1a6 at revision `f916f69f0ae570935991440712a08ad930469da3`, dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0:

| file | S′ (certificate side) | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `s344_amund.cert` | 9496283772422138783772412642309/500000000000000000000000000000 = 18.99256754484427… | `4e2c6880812a688a64c8f378f5feb27a8a1a362f0d9161c0cda201f444526e21` |
| `s344_amund.input.txt` | (float64, side 18.992567544825285) | `32cd4883edde91d300ef6b8f8cffc77972d2ad8ca1038101756f1ce8d2d233e5` |

A dilation certificate made with Evan Daniel's `search/packer/dilate_cert.py` at evand/square-packing `7982d7a9346e29e36cab3ce075274f3023114353` (macOS arm64, Python 3.14.6, Apple libm), from the input file; only the comment line was edited afterwards (a local path removed). Upper bound only.

**Checking.** At that commit, `python3 search/exact/verify_cert.py s344_amund.cert` (separating axes, exact rational): `VALID: s(n) <= S`, min wall clearance 6.054e-13, min pair separation 1.215e-12 (794 close pairs); `python3 search/exact/verify_cert2.py s344_amund.cert` (polygon intersection, exact): `VALID`, 794 close pairs; each about 1-2 s. Re-checked on the file downloaded from the gist. No full line of 19 upright squares (`layout.full_lines` = 0).

**What the checkers share.** Both are Evan Daniel's and share the certificate format, which was made with his `dilate_cert.py`; their geometry tests differ. Neither is ours.

**Not done.** No exact KKT solve, rigidity or local-optimality analysis.

**Lineage and credit.** A new packing of a different lineage from Couzo's 344: it is the register's 307 record design (Nate Chaoweeraprasit (itsnaka) / PingYou Ltd, PR #574; a 6+6 two-band family-A packing) stretched one K-step (one upright column plus one band square in each bottom-band row, and one upright row plus one band square in each left-band column; deficit 17 kept), starting from 307 minima of that design, then polished on the GPU (Apple Metal float32 batch of kicked variants, Evan Daniel's `fq` quench in 64-bit, iterated from the current best). Matched one-to-one against Couzo's 344 (optimal assignment, best of the eight square symmetries): max move 0.993, 67 squares move more than 0.1, 122 more than 0.01; tilted 114 vs 125. Credit: Amund Kristiansen, after the 307 design of Chaoweeraprasit / PingYou; the polish engine, certificate generator and checkers are Evan Daniel's.

**AI assistance.** Yes. As at #755 and #798: the search, the certificate and this report were done by Claude (Anthropic), working in Claude Code at my direction, using Evan Daniel's open-source engine and checkers.
